findings.claim: Rollback unconditionally closes a persisted context after implicit reconnect and action error
findings.scope: Existing persisted contexts are retained. Newly created unpersisted contexts still roll back on failed action, including after browser restart.

findings.claim: Historical context_recreated flag triggers rollback on later invalid launch
findings.scope: Rollback now queries actual unpersisted context ownership, not historical recreation.

findings.claim: No binding snapshot can make commit report success without durable context
findings.evidence: cross-family-no-target-red.log returns Ok after real Chrome target closure; cross-family-no-target-green.log
findings.scope: The test exercises commit helper with real Chrome events, not a whole command race. Existing persisted context with no target remains valid; fresh one fails and disposes.

findings.claim: Abrupt process death before persistence may leave unrecorded context
findings.scope: SIGKILL y corte de disposición medidos: huérfano remoto, sin contaminación sticky; cierre host observado. Sin garantía de crash-atomicity.

findings.claim: Binding-error response loses required lifecycle envelope
findings.evidence: actions.rs inject_lifecycle returns immediately for success!=true; existing error_response contract has id/success/error and optional tab_gone. Rollback clears browser before any tab_gone state can apply.
findings.scope: No promised lifecycle fields on error; no API change made.

findings.claim: CLI may omit isolateContext after removal of spawn env override
findings.evidence: main.rs attach_isolate_context_to_command called for main parsed command, CDP prelaunch, auto prelaunch, batch parsed command; compiled CLI suite was explicitly run with --ignored, including first failed request and successful connect/restart. DaemonState::new restores isolation from binding.
findings.scope: Actual user-defined isolation environment remains supported.

findings.claim: Chrome may ignore browserContextId when sent with page sessionId
findings.evidence: Real Chrome compiled CLI downloads preserve default and other context destinations and payload bytes. browser.rs other setDownloadBehavior call belongs only to BrowserManager::launch owned Chrome.
findings.scope: Dynamic evidence on macOS Chrome 152, not universal platform claim.

findings.claim: Browser download events could cross-talk between sessions
findings.evidence: Matching is unchanged by fix. Real simultaneous downloads and ten stress rounds passed with separate payload/directory oracles; missing-context mutation makes download test fail.
findings.scope: No forced hostile event interleaving injected. Timing coverage is evidence, not proof against every possible ordering.
